sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia. Munnar is a hill station in Kerala's Idukki District at ~1600m altitude. Tea estates dominate the landscape. All records needs_review.

places.name: Eravikulam National Park
places.description: National park and UNESCO World Heritage-listed Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve component, protecting the critically endangered Nilgiri tahr (mountain goat). Home to diverse high-altitude shola-grassland ecosystem. Neelakurinji flowers bloom every 12 years (next bloom ~2030). Only accessible to the Rajamala section; entry by shuttle bus from main gate.

places.name: Mattupetty Dam and Lake
places.description: Storage reservoir 13km from Munnar town at 1700m altitude, surrounded by tea and coffee plantations and shola forest. Boat rides on the lake available. The INDO-SWISS livestock project farm nearby raises high-quality dairy cattle. Good viewpoint and picnic site.

places.name: Tea Museum, Munnar
places.description: Museum operated by KDHP (Kanan Devan Hills Plantations) illustrating 150 years of tea cultivation in Munnar. Features vintage tea-processing machinery, plantation photographs and artefacts. Working factory attached showing the tea processing process. Informative context for the landscape before exploring the estates.

places.name: Top Station Viewpoint
places.description: Highest point on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border (1868m), 34km from Munnar. Offers sweeping views over the Munnar valley and tea estates into Tamil Nadu. Former top station of the Munnar-Kodai cable ropeway. Popular sunrise and sunset viewpoint. Road can be misty; drive carefully.

places.name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: Wildlife sanctuary 60km from Munnar at lower altitudes, home to elephant herds, grizzled giant squirrels, star tortoises and leopards. Contrasts sharply with Eravikulam's high-altitude grasslands; drier, hotter deciduous forest. Guided trekking available; permits required. Best Oct–May.

places.name: Anamudi Peak
places.description: South India's highest peak at 2695m, within Eravikulam National Park. Trekking to the summit requires prior permission from the Forest Department and is only possible in dry season. Multi-day planning needed; route not self-guided. For experienced trekkers only.
places.openingDays: Trekking permits required from Forest Dept; Dec–Apr only

places.name: Attukal Waterfalls
places.description: Series of small waterfalls 9km from Munnar town on the Munnar-Rajamala road, surrounded by shola forest. Not a large waterfall but set in scenic wooded surroundings. Swimming occasionally possible at the base during less crowded periods. Best after the monsoon (Oct–Dec).

places.name: Kolukkumalai Tea Estate
places.description: One of the world's highest tea estates (2100m), with an operating century-old factory accessible by a steep 10km mountain track from Suryanelli. Tea produced here is highly regarded. The off-road journey itself is an attraction; 4WD jeeps required from base. Half-day trip from Munnar.
places.openingDays: Factory: Mon–Sat; jeep tours on request

places.name: Munnar Tea and Spice Trail Café
places.description: High-altitude Munnar's tea estate cafés serve freshly brewed single-estate teas and locally grown cardamom and pepper. KTDC-run Santhigiri café at Top Station and TATA Tea Museum café are popular stops. Pair with banana fritters or puttu (steamed rice cake).
